name: Polyethylene terephthalate
process: Sorting → washing → shredding → flake purification → pelletising
notes: Clear beverage bottles are widely collected in many regions; coloured or multilayer PET may have narrower markets.
contamination: PVC labels, adhesives, oils and food residue can reduce flake quality.

name: High-density polyethylene
notes: Rigid natural and coloured HDPE containers are commonly mechanically recycled where collection exists.
contamination: Chemical residues, incompatible polymers and labels affect quality.

name: Low-density polyethylene
process: Film sorting → washing → drying → densifying → extrusion
notes: Film collection and recycling access is limited; clean, dry mono-material film is preferred.
contamination: Food, soil, paper labels and mixed laminates are problematic.

name: Polyvinyl chloride
process: Dedicated PVC sorting → contaminant removal → specialised reprocessing
notes: Requires dedicated streams because chlorine and additives can contaminate mixed-plastic recycling.
contamination: Mixing with PET or polyolefins can damage recycled output.

name: Polypropylene
notes: Rigid PP is increasingly recycled; local acceptance and product design matter.
contamination: Food residue, labels and mixed polymers reduce quality.

name: Polystyrene
process: Clean sorting → compaction or densification → specialised reprocessing
notes: Foamed PS is bulky and often lacks collection infrastructure.
contamination: Food contamination and low bulk density make collection uneconomic.

name: Aluminium
process: Sorting → de-coating → melting → alloy adjustment → casting
notes: Can be recycled repeatedly, but alloy separation and coatings affect output quality.
contamination: Steel attachments, plastics and mixed alloys require separation.

name: Steel
process: Magnetic separation → shredding → melting → refining → casting
notes: Ferrous scrap is widely recovered through magnetic separation.
contamination: Non-ferrous attachments, oils and hazardous coatings need management.

name: Copper
process: Cable stripping or sorting → granulation → smelting/refining
notes: High-value copper recovery depends on clean separation and grade.
contamination: Insulation, solder and mixed metal reduce grade.

name: Glass
process: Colour sorting → cleaning → crushing to cullet → remelting
notes: Container glass is recyclable where colour-separated collection exists.
contamination: Ceramics, stones, mirrors and heat-resistant glass are incompatible.

name: Paper
process: Sorting → pulping → screening → de-inking if needed → sheet forming
notes: Clean, dry paper can be repulped; wet-strength and coated grades may be difficult.
contamination: Oil, food, wax, plastic laminates and moisture reduce fibre recovery.

name: Corrugated cardboard
notes: Clean corrugated board is commonly recovered; keep dry and flatten for transport.
contamination: Grease, wet-strength coatings and excessive tape reduce quality.

name: Textile fibres
process: Sorting by fibre → reuse or mechanical/chemical fibre recovery
notes: Reuse is often preferable; fibre-to-fibre recycling depends on composition and blends.
contamination: Blended fibres, elastane, dyes and trims complicate recovery.

name: Rubber
process: Tyre or rubber sorting → shredding → crumb rubber/devulcanisation
notes: Specialist processors can produce crumb rubber; end markets and additives vary.
contamination: Steel cords, textiles and unknown additives need separation.

name: Wood
process: Sorting → de-nailing → chipping → panel or mulch manufacture
notes: Untreated clean wood is reusable or recyclable; treated/painted wood needs separate handling.
contamination: Preservatives, paints, laminates and fasteners limit reuse.

name: Electronic components (mixed)
process: Authorised collection → depollution → dismantling → mechanical/chemical metal recovery
notes: Use authorised e-waste handlers; batteries and circuit boards require controlled processing.
contamination: Battery damage, hazardous substances and mixed assemblies create safety risks.
